name: Miguel Juárez Celman

summary.text: Miguel Juárez Celman was President of Argentina from 1886 until his resignation on 6 August 1890 following the Revolution of the Park. His presidency coincided with a credit and investment boom that ended in the largest Argentine financial crisis of the nineteenth century and the London Baring crisis.

sources.publisher: Universidad Católica Argentina (Temas de Historia Argentina y Americana)
sources.title: Article on the 1890 crisis

facts.claim: The Revolution of the Park, which began with the seizure of the Buenos Aires Artillery Park in July 1890, was militarily defeated but achieved Juárez Celman's resignation on 6 August 1890; Vice-President Carlos Pellegrini succeeded him.
facts.quote: The financial crisis led to a deep recession, unemployment, and social discontent.

facts.claim: An Argentine academic article describes the boom unleashed during Juárez Celman's presidency as being followed by the largest Argentine financial crisis of the nineteenth century.
facts.quote: A partir de ese año cumbre del "boom" desatado durante la presidencia de Miguel Juárez Celman, sobreviene la mayor crisis financiera argentina del siglo XIX.

sources.publisher: Universidad Católica Argentina (Temas de Historia Argentina y Americana)
sources.title: Article on the 1890 crisis

facts.claim: Barings helped channel about £140 million of investment to Argentina between 1885 and 1890, the period covering Juárez Celman's presidency.
facts.quote: Serving as the leading investment bank for Argentina, Barings helped to channel £140 million of investment to Argentina between 1885 and 1890.

sources.publisher: Bank Underground (Bank of England staff blog)
sources.title: Rescuing a SIFI, Halting a Panic: the Barings Crisis of 1890

connections.claim: Baring Brothers was the leading investment bank channelling British capital to Argentina during Juárez Celman's presidency.

sources.publisher: Bank Underground (Bank of England staff blog)
sources.title: Rescuing a SIFI, Halting a Panic: the Barings Crisis of 1890

openQuestions: Site claim tested: his resignation after the 1890 Revolution of the Park is supported. The page's statements on paper-money expansion, inflation and a falling peso under his government were not addressed by the sources found.
